title: Customer escalation war-room — Cobalt Finance (payment timeouts) — 2026-04-11 notes
notes:
Context: Cobalt Finance reported increasing payment processing timeouts starting 2026-04-10 23:00 UTC. Customer impact: intermittent failed payments for ~12% of request volume (peak). They are on Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) with routing to us from eu-west-1. Customer oncall: Nadia (Cobalt).

Agenda (30m):
- Quick sync + current metrics (5m)
- Triage hypothesis + hands-on mitigations (15m)
- Customer comms + short-term SLA mitigation (5m)
- Assign action items + next checkpoint (5m)

Attendees: Maya (owner), Ethan (infra), Rosa (support eng), Liam (runtime), Kai (sre), Sofia (customer success), Nadia (Cobalt oncall - dialed in)

Timeline / What we know:
- 2026-04-10 23:00 UTC: first uptick in 5xx / timeouts reported by Cobalt metrics and our alerting.
- 2026-04-10 23:05 UTC: automated fallback to model-variant triggered for a subset of requests.
- 2026-04-10 23:15 UTC: Cobalt opened JIRA CS-1284 and flagged P0.
- 2026-04-11 00:10 UTC: partial recovery after routing change; but timeouts reappeared at 02:30 UTC.

Current status (as of 2026-04-11 09:00 UTC):
- Request success rate ~88% over last 1h; 12% still experiencing timeouts (mostly seq_len > 1024 requests).
- Latency tail (p95-p99) increased by 3x for a particular model variant (redwood-v2-legacy-quant).
- Dedicated pool utilization at 85%; some nodes showing high memory pressure.

Initial hypotheses:
1) KV-cache thrashing on long sequences leading to memory spills and GC on our runtime.
2) New client workload pattern from Cobalt (larger average seq_len) exposing a quantization edge-case in redwood-v2-legacy-quant kernels.
3) Network egress congestion between eu-west-1 availability zones causing retries/timeouts.

Evidence mapping:
- Hypothesis 1: memory pressure logs + OOM warnings observed on two nodes (Ethan).
- Hypothesis 2: error stack traces reference quantized kernel path for attention ops (Liam).
- Hypothesis 3: no cloud provider network-level alerts; packet drops not observed (Kai).

Immediate mitigations tried during call:
- Temporarily pinned Cobalt traffic to redwood-v2-std-nq (non-quant) for 20% of traffic — partial improvement.
- Increased autoscaling headroom by adding 2 GPUs to Dedicated pool (Ethan) — pending node spin-up (~12 min).
- Enabled stricter request size limits for the customer for new requests (Sofia coordinated with Nadia).

Customer comms (draft to send after next checkpoint):
- Short note acknowledging the issue, what we observed, immediate mitigation steps, ETA for next update (30m), promise to reduce failed payments and offer credits if SLA missed (TBD by BU). Keep tone empathetic and technical. (Sofia to send)

Decisions:
- Rollforward: keep redirected 20% on non-quant variant while we validate stability.
- No rollback to previous infra version at this time; prefer targeted kernel/fix and capacity increase.

Open questions / things to validate:
- Confirm whether Cobalt's client changed prompt sizes or sampling settings around 2026-04-10 (Sofia to confirm with Nadia).
- Full trace logs for one failed request to correlate stacktrace with memory events (Rosa/Liam).
- Confirm provider networking health for the specific AZs (Kai).

Notes to self (informal):
- Watch for any error patterns referencing aten:: or custom kernel names — often points to quant path.
- If autoscale nodes take >20m, escalate to infra-oncall.

meeting_summary: Short war-room to triage Cobalt Finance payment timeouts. Root cause unknown but evidence points at quantized kernel behaviour + memory pressure. Immediate actions: add capacity, redirect portion of traffic to non-quant variant, collect traces. Customer notified; next checkpoint in 30 minutes.
